references.text: The fulfillment of the prophecy: locusts covered the whole land so that the earth was darkened, just as Moses warned Pharaoh.
Locusts devouring crops are mentioned as a curse for disobedience to God, the same destruction as in Egypt.
Joel describes a plague of locusts that devours everything left, using similar imagery of total vegetation destruction.
God promises to restore what the locusts have eaten, reversing the type of destruction described in Exodus.
The psalmist recalls the locust plague in Egypt where they consumed all vegetation in the land, a poetic retelling of this event.
Reference to what survived the hail—the wheat and spelt that were not yet ripe—which were now to be devoured by the locusts.
Revelation describes locusts coming over the earth with destructive power, an eschatological echo of the plague in Egypt.
Part of the same plague sequence; shows the progression from hail (which leaves something) to locusts (which devour everything).
Thematic parallel: Deuteronomy uses the motif of plagues (total loss of crops) as a warning against breaking the covenant terms.
